around.headline: 'Phone-sticking and running' Metro trend raises safety concerns in Bengaluru
around.summary: A viral reel trend where people hold or tape a phone to a moving Metro train's window and run alongside it has reached Bengaluru, prompting safety warnings, per The Hindu. street_smart.title: A friend hands you their phone at a Bengaluru Metro platform and asks you to hold it against the train's window from outside as it starts moving, so they can get a viral 'phone-sticking and running' reel like the trend making news today. The doors are about to close. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: The Hindu, Sept 7 — a 'phone-sticking and running' Metro reel trend, where people hold or tape a phone to a moving train's window and run alongside it, has reached Bengaluru and is raising safety concerns. This mechanism hasn't been used as a street-smart scenario in the last three weeks.
street_smart.situation: Your friend says, 'It's fine, the train's barely moving right now — let go the second it speeds up.'

choices.text: Refuse, hand the phone straight back, and tell your friend to film from a stationary spot on the platform instead — no hand, phone, or bag ever touches a moving train.
choices.feedback: Correct. A train's starting speed is deceptive — it accelerates faster over the first few metres than most people judge, and platform gaps, closing doors, and a slick window ledge leave no safe moment to 'let go in time.' This is exactly why transit authorities have warned against and threatened action over this trend: the danger is in the physics, not the person's confidence.

choices.text: Do it, but only for the first second or two while the train still feels slow, planning to pull back well before it picks up real speed.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. 'It's still slow' is the exact assumption behind nearly every version of this stunt — grip on a window ledge can jam, and a moving train doesn't give a clear warning point between 'safe' and 'too fast.' Timing your reflexes against a machine that's accelerating is a bet you can lose in under a second.

choices.text: Agree to it, but only on an empty or off-peak platform, reasoning that fewer people around makes it safer.
choices.feedback: Risky. An empty platform doesn't change the physical risk of a fall or a caught hand — it only means fewer bystanders and staff nearby to react quickly if something goes wrong.

choices.text: Don't take part yourself, but stand back and film your friend doing it since it's their own choice to take the risk.
choices.feedback: Risky. Staying silent while watching someone attempt this doesn't remove your role — several transit authorities have said they'll act against participants and abettors alike. The safer move is to speak up or alert nearby Metro staff before it happens, not to document it after.

takeaways: Never attach anything — phone, hand, or bag strap — to a moving train from outside; there is no reliable moment to 'let go in time' once it starts accelerating.
If you see someone attempting a stunt like this on a platform, alert the nearest Metro staff rather than filming it or staying quiet.
Treat any viral trend involving a moving vehicle as riskier than it looks in the clip — the version that goes wrong rarely gets posted.

quiz.question: Bengaluru traffic police have announced road restrictions and diversions starting on which date, per today's advisory?
quiz.why: Advance traffic advisories give commuters time to plan alternate routes and avoid fines for entering a restricted stretch during the affected window.

quiz.question: Today's reported building collapse, with an FIR registered against the alleged owner, killed at least how many people?
quiz.why: Building collapses in dense Indian cities are frequently linked to unauthorised floor additions or ageing structures that never underwent a structural safety audit.

quiz.question: Which organisation today called reports of its privatisation 'completely baseless'?
quiz.why: ISRO operates as a department under the Government of India's Department of Space, not as a listed company, which is part of why privatisation claims about it keep resurfacing and getting denied.

quiz.question: Bengaluru's name officially changed from 'Bangalore' to 'Bengaluru' as part of a broader renaming of Karnataka cities. What is the state's name for this Kannada-language city called in English before that change?
quiz.why: Karnataka renamed several major cities to their Kannada-language forms in 2014, including Mysore to Mysuru and Mangalore to Mangaluru, alongside Bangalore to Bengaluru.

quiz.question: Which vitamin does the human body synthesize when skin is exposed to sunlight?
quiz.why: Vitamin D synthesis via sunlight is one reason prolonged indoor routines can lead to deficiency even in sunny cities like Bengaluru.
